properties.description:

rain over the Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute County. Between 0.5 and 1
inch of rain have fallen, with the heaviest rainfall occurring over

flash flooding in and around the Cottonwood Burn Scar in
Piute County, with flows impacting US 89 between mile
markers 171 to 176.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Cottonwood Burn Scar in Piute County.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
US 89 between mile markers 171 to 176 in.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 11 at 3:03PM EDT until August 11 at 6:15PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Athens County in southeastern Ohio...
Morgan County in southeastern Ohio...
Southern Perry County in southeastern Ohio...
Northwestern Washington County in southeastern Ohio...

* Until 615 PM EDT.

* At 303 PM EDT, Even though heavy rainfall has ended for now,
continued runoff will result in flash flooding of creeks and
streams. Additionally, thunderstorms may move back into the area
late this afternoon, further exacerbating the flooding situation.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Between 3 and 5 inches of rain fell from overnight
thunderstorms which resulted in flooding of some
structures, vehicles, and roads. This area is particularly
vulnerable to additional heavy rainfall. People should
remain vigilant into the early evening hours for
additional rises of creeks and streams.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Glouster, McConnelsville, Malta, Corning, Trimble, Burr Oak State
Park and Hackney.

Sunday Creek at Glouster was in minor flood with a stage of 15.5 feet
and slowly rising. At this stage, West Main Street and a portion of
Center Street flood in Glouster. In Jacksonville, Palmer Street near
the creek floods.
